msg: Google Custom Search JSON API endpoint. Google: closed to new customers; existing customers have until 2027-01-01 to transition.
msg_after: Google Custom Search JSON API endpoint. Google's transition date 2027-01-01 has passed; this call is on borrowed time.

msg: Google API client call to the Custom Search JSON API (same 2027-01-01 transition date as the raw endpoint).
fix: Replace the client with a plain HTTPS GET to /res/v1/web/search; Brave has no official Google-style discovery client

msg: Bing Search API v7 endpoint. Microsoft retired the Bing Search APIs on 2025-08-11.
Azure/Bing key header. Brave does not read this header, so the request goes out unauthenticated.
fix: Send the key as header X-Subscription-Token: <key>

msg: API key sent as the ?key= query parameter (Google style). Brave reads the key only from a header.
fix: Remove key from the query; add header X-Subscription-Token

msg: cx (Programmable Search Engine ID). Brave has no engine ID; the site list inside that engine is lost silently.
fix: Put the engine's sites into q as site:example.com operators, or use a Brave Goggle

msg: start = Google's 1-based result index (1, 11, 21 …). Brave offset is a 0-based PAGE index, max 9 — passing start through breaks page 2 onwards.
offset above 9. Brave's offset is a page index with a maximum of 9.
fix: Use a page index 0–9 (offset × count = results skipped)

msg: Page size above 20. Bing allowed count up to 50; Brave web search caps count at 20.
dateRestrict (d/w/m/y + N) has no Brave twin with the same name.
fix: freshness: pd | pw | pm | py, or a range YYYY-MM-DDtoYYYY-MM-DD for m6 / d3 etc.

msg: Bing freshness value (Day/Week/Month). Brave uses short codes.
fix: Day → pd · Week → pw · Month → pm

msg: siteSearch parameter. Brave has no siteSearch parameter.
Google safe= / Bing safeSearch= parameter. Brave's parameter is lowercase safesearch with its own values.
fix: safesearch: off | moderate | strict (Google active → strict)

msg: Google lr/gl/cr/hl or Bing mkt/setLang. Brave splits region and language into two parameters.
searchType=image on the web endpoint. Brave serves images from a separate endpoint.
Reads Google's items[] array. A Brave response has no items key — this returns undefined/KeyError, not an exception at the call.
Google result fields link/snippet. Brave results carry url and description.
fix: link → url · snippet → description · displayLink → meta_url.hostname

msg: Bing response path webPages.value[]. Brave uses web.results[] (name → title, snippet → description).
Total-hit count from Google/Bing. Brave returns no total count.
